description_ru: Organic deposits: fen (woody sedge peat 2-3 m) and peatland (sphagnum over sedge peat 0.5-4 m); pO-k with thermokarst
note: GSC Open File 4662 Surficial geology, Fort Norman NWT (2004), 1:250k, jp2 scan of a digital print. Organic 10-50 % of a unit is a red line overprint: grid = peat+fen, horizontal = fen, vertical = peat (--grid, pitch 26.3 px) -> index o/<base>, hclass2 O

description_ru: Alluvial floodplain and terraces: sand, gravel, silt; 2-5 m
Alluvial fans and floodplain-fan complexes: sand and silt, minor gravel, peat layers
Colluvial veneer (0-2 m) and slope complex: diamicton and rubble
Landslide deposits: rubble / diamicton (rotational slumps, retrogressive thaw flows, debris flows)
Eolian blanket, veneer, parabolic dunes: fine to medium sand
Glaciolacustrine plain (2-80 m) and veneer: silt and clay; Lp-k with thermokarst
Glaciolacustrine beach deposits: sand and gravel ridges
Lacustrine complex / transitional glaciofluvial-glaciolacustrine: sand over fines, 0-20 m
Lacustrine plain completely modified by mass wasting
Glaciofluvial outwash plains, terraces, veneer, deltas: sand and gravel
Ice-contact glaciofluvial: eskers, hummocks, kame complexes
Till veneer (< 2 m) and till plain conforming to topography
Drumlinoid / fluted till plain and till over streamlined bedrock
Coarse till: ridges (lateral moraines) and hummocks, up to 30 m
Till complex: hummocky, ridged or hilly with gravel patches
Colluvial talus of cryoplanation terraces: 1-3 m over bedrock
